summary: Round r1 (restricted network, defensive scope only). Benchmark design set out: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index pillars, national CERT mandate, sector incident-reporting obligations, data protection/breach notification, critical digital infrastructure resilience and reference standards (NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001/27035), with South Asian comparators. Only 8 document leads were located (ITU DataHub, ITU Facts and Figures 2025, NTA IT Policy 2023, National ICT Policy 2015, NITC/GIDC, secondary news) because the session's web-search budget was exhausted and itu.int/nist.gov are blocked; 11 key primary documents (incl. the GCI 2024 report and Nepal's National Cyber Security Policy 2080) are listed as unlocated with the exact data required. All empirical items pending.

findings.claim: Scope: defensive cybersecurity only - legal frameworks, incident-reporting and response capacity, standards adoption, critical digital infrastructure resilience and data protection. No offensive capability, vulnerability or targeting information is researched or recorded.

Benchmark design: Nepal's defensive posture is compared on (a) ITU GCI pillars (international, self-reported with ITU validation), (b) presence and mandate of a national CERT/CSIRT and sector CERTs, (c) incident-reporting obligations by sector (telecom, finance, government, energy), (d) data-protection law and breach-notification duty, (e) adoption of reference standards (NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001/27035), against South Asian comparators (India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan) and LDC peers.
Nepal ITU Global Cybersecurity Index result (tier and pillar scores) for the 2024 edition and earlier editions, with comparators.
findings.note: GCI report not located as a lead in r1 (search budget exhausted; itu.int blocked). Editions use different methods and scales - do not compare scores across editions without the methodology note.

findings.claim: Existence, legal basis and mandate of Nepal's national cyber security centre / CERT, and sectoral incident-reporting obligations (telecom, banking/payments, government data centre).
findings.note: Requires primary texts: National Cyber Security Policy 2080, NTA byelaw/IT policy, NRB guidelines. Only the NTA IT Policy (hosted copy) and ICT Policy 2015 located.

findings.claim: Nepal data-protection legal framework and breach-notification requirement.
findings.note: Individual Privacy Act 2075 and any data-protection bill; not located in r1.

findings.claim: Number of ISO/IEC 27001 certified organisations in Nepal and comparators.
findings.note: ISO Survey not located; catalog lacks an ISO id.

data_gaps: ITU GCI 2024 report and Nepal profile not located. The session-wide WebSearch budget was exhausted during this round; data-source hosts and reference hosts (itu.int, nist.gov, wikipedia.org, arxiv.org) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED to WebFetch.

Primary texts of Nepal's National Cyber Security Policy 2080, Individual Privacy Act 2075, Electronic Transactions Act 2063, NTA cyber byelaw and NRB cyber guidelines not located (see specific.defensive_posture_benchmarks.unlocated_documents).
No incident statistics for Nepal located (national CERT reports).
Catalog lacks ids for NIST, ISO, FIRST, Council of Europe and Nepal Telecommunications Authority.

assumptions.text: Research is limited to defensive posture; no offensive or vulnerability-specific content is collected.
GCI scores are self-reported questionnaire results validated by ITU and are treated as a posture indicator, not a measure of realised security outcomes.

challenges.text: X36 is mapped to channel digital_services_demand only; cyber incidents also affect payments (remittance channel) and critical infrastructure (energy, aviation). Consider mapping X36 to additional channels.

Supports your note to 28: the single-gateway telecom/internet backbone via India/China should be a proposed exposure entry; 24D will supply defensive-resilience evidence once route data (NTA) are located.
Search budget exhausted; allocate searches or a network-enabled run for 24D in r2. Add catalog ids for nta_nepal, nist, iso, first, coe.
Red-team: GCI tier changes across editions reflect method changes as well as policy changes; audit any claim of 'improvement' against the methodology notes.

uncertainty: Very high. Most primary documents were not located in r1; titles of Nepal instruments and standards in unlocated_documents are from domain knowledge and unverified. GCI is self-reported and methods differ by edition. No incident data.

defensive_posture_benchmarks.question: What defensive standards and incident-reporting frameworks are relevant to Nepal?
defensive_posture_benchmarks.answer_r1: Partially answered at design level, pending on evidence. Relevant frameworks are identified by type: the ITU GCI five-pillar benchmark; reference defensive standards (NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27035, FIRST CSIRT Services Framework); Nepal's own instruments (National Cyber Security Policy 2080, Electronic Transactions Act 2063, Individual Privacy Act 2075, NTA and NRB sector rules); and comparator incident-reporting regimes (EU NIS2, India CERT-In directions). Most primary documents were NOT located as URLs in r1 and are listed under unlocated_documents with the exact data required; titles are recorded from domain knowledge and must be verified.
